newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - April 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - April 9.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on April 9:

WASHINGTON - The Internal Revenue Service fired 23 employees, disciplined 349 and counseled 472 others after agency audits found that government computers were still being used to browse through the tax records of friends, relatives and celebrities.
LOS ANGELES - A federal appeals court panel, siding with opponents of affirmative action, upheld California's voter-approved ban on preferences based on race and gender.

HEBRON, West Bank - Another round of ferocious clashed broke out on the West Bank, leaving three Palestinians dead and adding to growing evidence that a violent uprising has resumed alongside the dead-locked peace process.

WASHINGTON - Despite President Clinton's public rebuke of the FBI, senior administration officials say they have concluded that White House personnel and procedures bear significant responsibility for a breakdown in communications that left Clinton unaware of an investigation into suspected Chinese influence-buying.
WASHINGTON - The Clinton administration has been pressing Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko to resign and go into exile to help achieve a peaceful settlement of the civil war there.

WASHINGTON - In the month before Jack Kent Cooke's death Sunday, representatives of the Washington Redskins owner contacted several major companies about buying the right to put their name on Cooke's new stadium, but his son wants the facility to bear his father's name.

WASHINGTON - Twenty-five years after the end of the infamous Tuskegee experiment, the United States plans to formally apologize to the few remaining survivors and relatives of almost 400 impoverished African American men who were left untreated for syphilis as part of a government study.
